programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey, a lively and creative puppy, transforms every day into an adventure for her family, thanks to her fertile imagination and endless energy.
programme.desc-more: This funny and sincere look at modern family life celebrates how creative games help to shape children. Bluey, an Australian puppy-poy, has a mind-blowing imagination and loves to turn daily life into fun adventures. She and her little sister Bingo are embarking on exploring their world, using the game to overcome their fears and try to play adult roles. They are more pleased with nothing than to train their parents, especially their father, in their games. Mom, Chilli, went back to work, and Dad, Bandit, juggles between child care and telework. But if he thinks he's the one who commands it, it's the girls who lead the dance when it comes to playing, but also for everything else!

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Dad had the rudeness to sit at one end of the swing. Bluey and Bingo go around the playground to find help to get him down, but they need more help to get there.
programme.desc-more: In the colorful and sparkling world of Bluey, a young blue bitch, the daily adventure takes a playful and imaginative turn. Accompanied by her little sister Bingo, Bluey transforms everyday situations into captivating games. When Bluey receives an invitation to a birthday party, the excitement is at its peak. However, Bingo, with his magical pen, complicates the preparations by introducing unexpected and fanciful elements that test the patience of the whole family. At the same time, their father, Bandit (David McCormack), is confronted with the challenges of daily life when he has to drive his daughters to school. The two little bitches, with their overly creativeness, will not fail to imagine hilarious and surprising scenarios, making each moment memorable. Through games that reflect their daily lives, Bluey and Bingo learn valuable lessons about friendship, family and imagination, while bringing joy and laughter to those around them.

programme.title: Looking for Cézanne
programme.desc: In the 1930s, three men, two Germans and one Italian, became passionate about Paul Cézanne's work, whose catalogue they had prepared.
programme.desc-more: In the early 1930s, three foreigners, two Germans and one Italian, became passionate about Paul Cézanne's work, which had disappeared in 1906. When Léo Marchutz, the painter, Lionello Venturi, the art critic, and John Rewald, the student photographer, meet in Provence, they immediately set out on the traces of the great master. Wanting to understand everything about his technique and his influences, they become the best specialists and seal a flawless friendship there. Before them, no one had consulted the archives, no one had looked at the painter's gesture, his motives, his colours, no one had gone to check the source of his writings.

programme.title: She Said
programme.desc: Despite various threats, two young New York Times journalists managed to collect evidence that compromised a Hollywood laying.
programme.desc-more: In 2016, two New York Times journalists, Megan Twohey (Carey Mulligan) and Jodi Kantor (Zoe Kazan), are attacking a burning issue that will upset the entertainment industry and society. While Megan investigates Donald Trump's inappropriate behavior towards several women, Jodi focuses on the actions of producer Harvey Weinstein, whose abuses have long been in the shadows. Despite interviews with some actresses, Jodi is encountering increasing reluctance, many fearing reprisals for speaking. Aware of the issues at stake, she sought Megan's help, hoping to find strategies to advance her investigation. Together, they discover a network of silence and complicity, highlighting the challenges faced by women who dare to denounce abuses. Their bold investigation becomes the catalyst for a movement that will transform the perception of sexual violence in the world of cinema and beyond.

programme.desc-more: This funny and sincere look at modern family life celebrates how creative games help to shape children. programme.desc: As Mom ends reading her a story and wishes her good night by kissing her, Bingo promises her that tomorrow morning she will wake up in her own bed.
programme.desc-more: In the colorful and sparkling world of Bluey, a young blue bitch, the daily adventure takes a playful and imaginative turn. Accompanied by her little sister Bingo, Bluey transforms everyday situations into captivating games. When Bluey receives an invitation to a birthday party, the excitement is at its peak. However, Bingo, with his magical pen, complicates the preparations by introducing unexpected and fanciful elements that test the patience of the whole family. At the same time, their father, Bandit (David McCormack), is confronted with the challenges of daily life when he has to drive his daughters to school. The two little bitches, with their overly creativeness, will not fail to imagine hilarious and surprising scenarios, making each moment memorable. Through games that reflect their daily lives, Bluey and Bingo learn valuable lessons about friendship, family and imagination, while bringing joy and laughter to those around them.

programme.title: Simon Superlapin
programme.desc: Superlapin is trying to convince his little brother, Captain Rabbit, that ghosts do not exist and that you must not be afraid, but it is not an easy mission.
programme.desc-more: In this captivating episode of season 2 of "Simon Superlapin", the excitement is at its peak as Simon (voice of the actor), Lou (voice of the actor) and Ferdinand (voice of the actor) prepare to present a show in front of all the parents. Costumes and energy overflowing, the three friends are determined to deliver a memorable performance. However, pressure rises when Ferdinand, panicked, realizes that he will be the first to enter the stage. His growing anxiety overwhelms him and he begins to decompose, fearing to find himself alone in front of the audience. The other characters try to reassure him and motivate him, but Ferdinand's fear threatens to compromise the long-awaited spectacle. Through moments of camaraderie, hesitation and mutual support, this episode explores the themes of friendship, courage and perseverance, while promising unexpected twists and life lessons.

programme.title: Peppa Pig
programme.desc: Peppa is a little girl who is a little impertinent and sometimes authoritarian. She lives with her parents and her little brother George. Like all his fellows, his favorite hobby is to jump all over the mud puddles, groan and laugh. George and Peppa discover the world with great eyes amazed and at the same time learn all the words to make themselves understood. So, Dad Pig's office, or the painting, fruits or fish have no secrets for them anymore.
programme.desc-more: Peppa is a little slut full of life and energy, always ready to explore the world around her. With his little brother George (Lily Snowden-Fine), they are living thrilling and fun adventures alongside their parents, Mom Pig and Papa Pig (Richard Ridings). Peppa loves jumping into mud puddles, an activity that gives him immense joy and symbolizes his mischievous spirit. Each episode takes them into a variety of situations, whether on a farm trip, a day at the beach, or even a simple visit to friends. Through these moments of play and discovery, Peppa and George learn valuable lessons about friendship, family and sharing. Colourful characters, such as their friend Suzy Sheep (Morwenna Banks) and the teacher, add a touch of magic to their daily lives, making each episode both educational and entertaining.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: It's Halloween! Everyone is disguised: Bing is a Croquosaurus, Sula is a fairy unicorn, Pando is a pirate, Coco is a mean queen and Charlie is a cute hedgehog! But what happens when Bing tries to do "Bouh!" to Charlie?
programme.desc-more: In a world full of bright colours and joy, the Teletubes, small, joyful creatures with vibrant hues, spend their days exploring their peaceful landscape. Each one of them, with its unique personality, engages in fun and interactive activities, learning to discover and appreciate the world around them. Tinky Winky, the tallest, wears a mysterious pouch, while Dipsy, with his green hat, likes to dance and play. The sweet Laa-Laa, always accompanied by her ball, and the curious Po, the smallest of the group, add their touch of innocence to their adventures. Through games, laughter and moments of wonder, Teletubbies learn valuable lessons about friendship and sharing. Each episode is punctuated with the appearance of their ventral television screen, which broadcasts captivating videos of small children playing and having fun, thus reinforcing the idea that joy is found in daily interactions and discoveries.

programme.title: Chicken mania
programme.desc: From farms to supermarket shelves, star-starred kitchens to the madness of chicken crousty, investigation of the French's favorite meat and the hidden face of chicken mania.
programme.desc-more: Whether roasted, cut, chopped, breaded, fried or grilled, chicken has made a place of choice in French plates. In 2024, he rose to the rank of meat most consumed in Hexagon. Cheap, high in protein, low in fat, it is folded to all desires and all purses. But behind this true French passion are the shadows of the world: opacity on the conditions of farming, risks related to ultra-processed products, labels of all kinds and low-cost imports. How do I recognize a "good" chicken?

programme.title: Dora, the giant young otter
programme.desc: In Brazil, four young giant otters are coming out of their den for the first time and learn the rules of survival in a hostile nature.
programme.desc-more: A family of giant otters lives on the banks of the Vermelho River in Brazil. The four young ones are coming out of their den for the first time. They will have to quickly become excellent swimmers, able to catch their own meals. One of the young males enthusiastically launched, but he soon learned that he had to remain on guard if he did not want to become prey to a caiman or jaguar. Other family members will protect the young people and teach them what they will need to survive in this hostile nature.

programme.title: The roads of the impossible
programme.desc: In Burundi, cyclists carrying banana regimes and people working in mines brave all the obstacles to earning a living.
programme.desc-more: In Burundi, the country with the lowest average income in the world, people are prepared to take all risks on the roads to earn a living. Kamikaze cyclists travel the roads at all speed to sell their bananas on the market. Attracted by economic opportunities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, some Burundians embark on extreme travel. In this country where three out of ten children are forced to work, mining the minerals hidden in its basements could soon change the situation.

programme.title: Beautiful escapes
programme.desc: Ismaël Khelifa surveys the sea coast and the hinterland of the Hérault department, meeting people who embody a true harmony with the landscapes they inhabit, whether it is an ostrianist of the pond of Thau or a scientist vograting on the Mediterranean.
programme.desc-more: From the seafront to the more secret landscapes of the hinterland, from Sète to the lake of Thau, to the natural circus of Navacelles, Ismaël Khelifa offers a beautiful escape in the Hérault. The globe-trotter will discover this department by going to meet people who love this land and who have decided to take care of it while it is increasingly visited, especially in summer by tourists. It is the third favorite destination of the French. In summary: One day in Sète. The maritime heritage of Sète. Biodiversity of the Thau pond. The tambourine game. Water management.

programme.title: Beautiful escapes
programme.desc: With renewable energies, eco-districts and sustainable resource management, Denmark is a model of ecology. Jérôme Pitorin is trying to understand how the country has built such a harmony between nature, modernity and strong identity and to decipher what makes the Danish model singular.
programme.desc-more: Jérôme Pitorin explores Denmark and its 7,300 km of coastline that have shaped its deep sea-facing traditions and identity. The traces of their ancestors the Vikings can be found all over the country, especially in this attachment to the ocean and the environment which today make Denmark a model of ecology. Between Copenhagen, Møn Island, the Wadden Sea and the South Fionian archipelago, Jérôme Pitorin discovers this unique culture through memorable encounters.

programme.title: Peppa Pig
programme.desc: Peppa is a little girl who is a little impertinent and sometimes authoritarian. She lives with her parents and her little brother George. Like all his fellows, his favorite hobby is to jump all over the mud puddles, groan and laugh. George and Peppa discover the world with great eyes amazed and at the same time learn all the words to make themselves understood. So, Dad Pig's office, or the painting, fruits or fish have no secrets for them anymore.
programme.desc-more: Peppa is a little slut full of life and energy, always ready to explore the world around her. With his little brother George (Lily Snowden-Fine), they are living thrilling and fun adventures alongside their parents, Mom Pig and Papa Pig (Richard Ridings). Peppa loves jumping into mud puddles, an activity that gives him immense joy and symbolizes his mischievous spirit. Each episode takes them into a variety of situations, whether on a farm trip, a day at the beach, or even a simple visit to friends. Through these moments of play and discovery, Peppa and George learn valuable lessons about friendship, family and sharing. Colourful characters, such as their friend Suzy Sheep (Morwenna Banks) and the teacher, add a touch of magic to their daily lives, making each episode both educational and entertaining.

Each episode follows Bluey's games and interactions with her father, Bandit (David McCormack), and her mother, Chilli (Melanie Zanetti), who encourage her creative spirit while teaching her valuable life lessons. Whether it's transforming itself into a fearless explorer or organizing improvised shows, Bluey turns everyday situations into extraordinary adventures. The episodes also highlight relationships with her little sister, Bingo, and her friends, illustrating the challenges and joys of childhood. Through touching and humorous narratives, the series addresses universal themes such as friendship, family and imagination, captivating an audience of all ages.

programme.title: Peppa Pig
programme.desc: Today, Peppa and her family watch television... until it breaks down! They ask Grampy Rabbit if he can fix it. Meanwhile, the family receives a new television that can do anything but it's not worth their old TV. So when their old TV is fixed, they send the new TV back to the store!
programme.desc-more: Peppa is a little mischievous slut who shares her daily life with her family in a colorful and playful world. Surrounded by her little brother George, Mom Pig and Papa Pig, she explores the world around her with curiosity and enthusiasm. Both children embark on daily adventures, whether they jump into mud puddles, visit the zoo or play with their friends. Through fun and sometimes nasty situations, Peppa and George discover the simple joys of life, learning to express their emotions and develop their vocabulary. The themes of friendship, family and learning are at the heart of each episode, offering young spectators valuable lessons while entertaining them. The series, which won a BAFTA Award in 2005 for its quality of animation, continues to captivate children from all over the world with its endearing characters and fantasy stories.

programme.title: The future of the Great Barrier Reef
programme.desc: Australia is the world's largest coral reef: the Great Barrier. There are processes as magical as they are threatened by global warming.
programme.desc-more: Under the surface of the Coral Sea, off the Australian Queensland, stands the world's largest coral reef, the Great Barrier. Every year, the arrival of spring in this underwater environment generates the magnificent and fragile reproduction of coral. More than 60,000 sea turtles are heading to Raine Island to make it the largest spawning site in the world. Processes as magical as they are threatened by global warming. This documentary offers us an immersive journey into the frenzy of the beginning of life, accompanied by enlightening explanations from local marine explorers and curators.

programme.desc-more: In the Alps, Jérôme Pitorin embarks on a summer trip to the heart of the Massif des Aravis, located on horseback between Haute-Savoie and Savoie. programme.title: The fabulous history of birds, dinosaurs among us
programme.desc: Daniel Field, a specialist in paleo-ornithology at Cambridge University, is working on the reconstruction of the major stages of bird evolution, the last survivors of the disaster that led to the extinction of their cousins dinosaurs. In 2019, he found in a fossil the crane of the oldest modern bird ever discovered. Now, research focuses on the reasons for their survival for millions of years and on their colonization of our planet. However, many of the 11,000 species of birds that inhabit the Earth today are threatened with extinction.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Dad's trying to teach Bluey to play chess, but Mom thinks she's too young. When Bingo joins the game, the girls invent their own rules.
programme.desc-more: This funny and sincere look at modern family life celebrates how creative games help to shape children. Bluey, an Australian puppy-poy, has a mind-blowing imagination and loves to turn daily life into fun adventures. She and her little sister Bingo are embarking on exploring their world, using the game to overcome their fears and try to play adult roles. They are more pleased with nothing than to train their parents, especially their father, in their games. Mom, Chilli, went back to work, and Dad, Bandit, juggles between child care and telework. But if he thinks he's the one who commands it, it's the girls who lead the dance when it comes to playing, but also for everything else!

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey and Bingo play silent. They don't want to talk to Dad about what toy to buy. He eventually asked Alfie, the new employee, to help him to de-enact the girls' mimes.
programme.desc-more: In the colorful and sparkling world of Bluey, a young blue bitch, the daily adventure takes a playful and imaginative turn. Accompanied by her little sister Bingo, Bluey transforms everyday situations into captivating games. When Bluey receives an invitation to a birthday party, the excitement is at its peak. However, Bingo, with his magical pen, complicates the preparations by introducing unexpected and fanciful elements that test the patience of the whole family. At the same time, their father, Bandit (David McCormack), is confronted with the challenges of daily life when he has to drive his daughters to school. The two little bitches, with their overly creativeness, will not fail to imagine hilarious and surprising scenarios, making each moment memorable. Through games that reflect their daily lives, Bluey and Bingo learn valuable lessons about friendship, family and imagination, while bringing joy and laughter to those around them.

programme.title: Simon Superlapin
programme.desc: Superlapin doesn't like losing, especially against Professor Wolf. He will never abandon a mission, because as a real superhero, Superlapin always finds a solution.
programme.desc-more: In this thrilling episode of the series "Simon Superlapin", our eponymous hero, Superlapin, finds himself facing a major challenge: facing the formidable Professor Wolf, a genius of evil who does not retreat in front of anything to sow chaos. Superlapin, who embodies the spirit of determination and optimism, categorically refuses to let himself be defeated by adversity. Each mission he undertakes is marked by his unwavering willingness to find a solution, no matter what the obstacles. While Professor Wolf is implementing a Machiavellical plan to take control of the city, Superlapin must bring together his friends, such as his faithful acolyte, Simon, and other colorful characters, to thwart the wicked's plans. Through a series of hilarious adventures and puzzles to solve, Superlapin proves that with courage and ingenuity, it is possible to overcome even the most desperate situations.

programme.title: Peppa Pig
programme.desc: Mom Pig buys her daughter a pair of shoes. Peppa loves them until she wants to leave them. When the whole family plays in the mud puddles of the garden, Peppa always wears her new shoes...
programme.desc-more: Peppa is a little mischievous and life-filled pig who shares her colorful universe with her little brother George, their mom Pig and their dad Pig. Together, they explore the world around them with curiosity and joy. Peppa loves to have fun, whether playing hide and seek, disguised as princesses or jumping in mud puddles, which gives him immense pleasure. Each episode highlights Peppa's and her family's daily adventures, while introducing a gallery of endearing characters, such as her friends Rebecca Rabbit and Suzy Mouton. Through simple situations and life lessons, Peppa learns essential values such as friendship, sharing and creativity. With its humor and good, contagious mood, Peppa invites young spectators to discover the world with a wonderful look, while cultivating their imagination.

programme.title: Trains like the others
programme.desc: Philippe Gougler explores the landscapes of the island of Spitzberg and the Lofoten in June, when the sun never sets.
programme.desc-more: Philippe Gougler begins his journey to the Svalbard archipelago on the island of Spitzberg, a remote island where time seems to have stopped. He met a woman pastor who explained life in this isolated region of the North Pole. It continues on the city of Longyearbyen the most northerly city in the world. He is not at the end of his surprises when he discovered the ghost town of Pyramidn, the Soviet mining town that is the remnant of the USSR. Its stopover stops on the continent with a return to a greener landscape in Lonsdal and then to the islands of Lofoten known for salmon fishing.

programme.title: Beautiful escapes
programme.sub-title: The Cevennes, a return to the sources
programme.desc: The territory of the Cevennes covers four massifs: Mount Lozère, Causse-Méjean, the Cevenole valleys and Mount Aigoual. It is the only French National Park inhabited. It offers remarkable landscapes shaped by man and nature. Its assets are increasingly attracting supporters of a simpler life.
programme.desc-more: Located in the Central Massif, the Cevennes offer exceptional places surrounded by large preserved natural spaces. A destination of choice for those who support a simpler life, wishing to get away from the big cities. This territory, forming a mountain range, has its National Park, the only one inhabited in France. The park, along with a large part of the Cevennes, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Subjects: Stevenson's Road History • Made in Cevennes • Change of life • Here it is the Cevennes • Wildlife • Living in isolation.

programme.title: At the end it's the sea
programme.desc: François Pécheux sails on the 1000 kilometers of the Loire, the longest river in France, from its source in Ardèche to its estuary in Saint-Nazaire.
programme.desc-more: François Pécheux travels the longest river in France, the Loire, from the Mont Gerbier-de-Jonc, in Ardèche, to the estuary of Saint-Nazaire, where it flows into the Atlantic Ocean. 1,000 km down on a fierce and always unpredictable beauty. The globe-trotter meets enthusiastic guardian angels, solitary freshwater sailors but also well-drained characters and lovers of the Loire River. The journey begins at the foot of thousands of thousand-year-old volcanoes of the Central Massif, where we follow shy balloon meanders. Then the river widens to canoe.

programme.title: C tonight
programme.desc: From Monday to Thursday, "C tonight" gives the floor to researchers, artists and intellectuals from all walks of life. The program is built around a political or social subject that has made the news of the day. This debate allows us to deepen our reflection on this event with the aim of enlightening the complexity of the world.
programme.desc-more: With French people more concerned than ever about the repercussions of the various political, health, social, economic, energy and war crises in Ukraine and the Middle East, intellectuals, artists and protagonists at the centre of the news come to bring their expertise to a debate. Karim Rissouli and Camille Diao, accompanied either by Laure Adler or Arthur Chevallier, receive several guests who provide answers to the questions that are topical while revealing their ideas. Ideas are the stars of this event, which highlights a diversity of views on the complexity of the world.

programme.title: Second hand... first of class?
programme.desc: Repairing rather than throwing and "upcycling" rather than buying new, the circular economy is becoming more and more popular with the French.
programme.desc-more: The second hand has the wind in France. In Saint-Herblain, private individuals sell their effects in a covered attic vacuum, year round. Romain Chassagne, a brocante lover, imported this concept from Finland, and opened about 60 brands across the country. Other shops sell the products by kilo. Beyond the used clothing, the second hand touches other sectors: luxury, building, household appliances... But this market is not always virtuous, and the circular economy also has its shortcomings.

In this colorful universe, they cross the path of Professor Wolf (voice of an actor), an eccentric inventor who is hard at creating a robot designed to facilitate the picking of strawberries. However, the intervention of Mamie Wolf (a voice of an actor) complicates the situation, as she is concerned about the safety of her grandson, convinced that he is still too young to handle machines. This playful adventure questions the notion of maturity and the relation to the limits imposed by adults.

This episode promises to explore themes of prejudice and self-discovery, while offering moments of lightness and humour that characterize the series.

programme.title: Men of influence
programme.desc: A few weeks before the elections, the US president, accused of rape, organized a media manipulation with the help of a specialist.
programme.desc-more: A disaster in the White House a few weeks before the elections: the president of the United States is accused of rape of a majorette. The media is taking over the case, the scandal is huge. Conrad Brean, special advisor to the president and great media manipulation professional, is called to the rescue. Assisted by Winifred Ames, the President's private adviser, Brean sets up a smokescreen in front of the President, who he carefully keeps abroad, by making rumours about a possible war with Albania. Shortly thereafter, the Special Advisor contacted Stanley Mots, a renowned Hollywood producer, and entrusted him with the task of producing images of this fictitious war.

programme.title: Catherine Leroy, a French woman in the Vietnam War
programme.desc: At 21, without experience, young photographer Catherine Leroy left alone to cover the Vietnam War. His photographs are of a staggering depth.
programme.desc-more: Catherine Leroy was one of the few women photographers who covered the Vietnam War between 1966 and 1968. At 21, she had no experience, and decided to leave everything to go as close to the hostilities as possible. His photos, of a staggering proximity, tell of a war seen by a fearless young woman who, alone among soldiers of her age, was able to capture the reality of combat with force and humanity. While Vietnam was its first land, it continued its work on other fronts until the 1990s. Catherine Leroy imposed her look before being forgotten.

This episode highlights the themes of acceptance, friendship and misunderstandings, while exploring the humorous and sometimes conflicting dynamics between these two endearing characters. programme.title: Simon Superlapin
programme.sub-title: Super Elvis is just at his head
programme.desc: In this humorous episode of the series "Simon Superlapin", Simon (Superlapin) and Gaspard (Captain Rabbit) embark on a bold mission: to train Elvis, the mischievous dog of their grandparents. Despite Papi's encouragement, who assures that this dog is a great dog capable of understanding much more than it seems, Elvis seems to be only at his head, stubbornly refusing to give his "pattte". In the face of this frustrating situation, the two brothers decided to turn into a superhero to convince their four-legged companion to listen to them. They dive into their imaginary world and face an unexpected challenge: even as Superlapin and Captain Rabbit, Elvis remains indifferent to their orders. Through this fun adventure, children discover that patience and understanding are sometimes the best weapons to connect with their hair friends.

programme.title: Beautiful escapes
programme.sub-title: Scotland, the magic of the Highlands
programme.desc: From the mythical Loch Ness to the forests of Perthshire, through Inverness, the largest city in the Highlands, Kerrera Island and the charming port of Oban, Sophie Jovillard travels the north of Scotland. The presenter goes on a journey to meet the guardians of the identity of this mountainous region, which has more sheep than inhabitants. These "Beautiful Escapes" reveal landscapes as wild as they are spectacular, dotted with castles and lakes and bordered by paradise beaches.

programme.title: Beautiful escapes
programme.sub-title: The Cevennes, a return to the sources
programme.desc: Located in the Central Massif, the Cevennes offer exceptional places surrounded by large preserved natural spaces. A destination of choice for those who support a simpler life, wishing to get away from the big cities. This territory, forming a mountain range, has its National Park, the only one inhabited in France. The park, along with a large part of the Cevennes, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Subjects: Stevenson's Road History • Made in Cevennes • Change of life • Here it is the Cevennes • Wildlife • Living in isolation.

programme.title: Trains like the others
programme.desc: Philippe Gougler starts his trip to Norway, on a train whose route is ranked among the most beautiful in the world. Norway has more than a thousand fjords. These stone giants sculpt the geography of the country and keep the latest Viking secrets.

programme.title: Johnny Hallyday symphonic
programme.desc: Yvan Cassar was the master of the "Johnny Hallyday Symphony" tour, the first of which took place at the Acropolis of Nice in 2022. In this large-scale project, Johnny Hallyday's historic artistic director was aiming to revive the singer's artistic world on stage by making his voice heard accompanied by 100 musicians. A "foul" idea, which now allows you to rediscover your greatest titles in a new symphonic version. Yvan Cassar does not derogate from any rule of the past: fidelity to the tastes of the artist, musical rigor, splendour of the set.

programme.title: At the end it's the sea
programme.desc: Discover the summary of the episodes of season 5 of the series At the end it is the sea

programme.title: The Docs of La Grande Librairie
programme.desc: Victor Hugo is an undisputed figure of French literature, and he is a name that resonates throughout the centuries. Whether it is through his novels, their countless adaptations or the ubiquitous references to his work, he left an indelible imprint in literary history. But Hugo was not only a writer, he was also a man of political commitment, a defender of the oppressed, whose ideals permeate his works and give them a resonance that traverses the generations. His life, marked by dramatic events, and his exceptional longevity nourished his legend, propelling his influence far beyond his time.

programme.title: C policy
programme.desc: Thomas Snegaroff welcomed viewers to decipher the news and tell the story of the time. Around him, for this presidential year, two new faces: Blanche Leridon, essayist and editorial director of the Institut Montaigne, and Raphaël Llorca, associate expert at the Fondation Jean-Jaurès. These two opinion specialists decipher the aspirations, fears and hopes of French and French people during this historic presidential campaign. They are also alongside Thomas to interview intellectuals, witnesses, women and men who question or move society.

programme.title: C policy, the future
programme.desc: In the face of the important issues that go through our times, the show offers a space for analysis and exchange between experts, citizens and philosophers. The objective: to decipher the major contemporary topics in order to help us understand them better.

programme.title: The factory of lies
programme.sub-title: Hollywood and women, the empire of silence
programme.desc: Almost ten years after the #MeToo movement came into existence, this survey demonstrates how Hollywood continues to stifle women's speech. If the system has been flickering, it has not disappeared, but reorganized. Today, to silence actresses, a new method has become necessary: online denigration campaigns. The actress Blake Lively was victimized after she denounced the atmosphere of one of her films. From hundreds of private exchanges, from the audience of the actress and the man she accuses, the investigation reveals the workings of a new economy of influence, in which press attachés, crisis communicators, bloggers, youtubers and influencers can help shape, and sometimes destroy, a reputation.

programme.title: On behalf of the lost children
It's up to you.
programme.sub-title: Moms solos, the heart for guide
programme.desc: Anaïs, 29, and Alexandra, 54, two single, blind mothers, share their lively daily life, between troubleshooting and mutual help.

programme.title: Flights to Italy
programme.desc: Walk in the heart of South Italy, starting from the region of Campania and its famous capital, Naples, and passing through the ruins of Pompeii dominated by Vesuvius.

programme.title: A year on Earth
programme.desc: The scientists, ecologists and local populations involved are essential to preserving the incredible diversity and beauty of wildlife. Technological innovations allow them to discover previously unknown behaviors. Aware of the pressure exerted by human activities on the natural world, they do not hesitate to risk their lives to preserve the future of the planet. Their research follows the rhythm of nature's transformations throughout a year on earth.

programme.title: Pompeii's great puzzle
programme.desc: Artificial intelligence was used to rebuild the past of Pompeii, an ancient city buried by a violent eruption of Vesuvius in the year 79. For the first time, computer scientists, robotic engineers, archaeologists and historians are testing revolutionary technology for one of the most complex tasks of archaeology: the physical reconstruction of broken works of art. Focus on this process and, above all, on the outcome of this long-term work.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: This funny and sincere look at modern family life celebrates how creative games help to shape children. She and her little sister Bingo are embarking on exploring their world, using the game to overcome their fears and try to play adult roles. They are more pleased with nothing than to train their parents, especially their father, in their games. Mom, Chilli, went back to work, and Dad, Bandit, juggles between child care and telework. But if he thinks he's the one who commands it, it's the girls who lead the dance when it comes to playing, but also for everything else!

programme.title: Peppa Pig
programme.desc: Peppa is a little mischievous slut who shares her daily life with her family in a colorful and playful world. Surrounded by her little brother George, Mom Pig and Papa Pig, she explores the world around her with curiosity and enthusiasm. Both children embark on daily adventures, whether they jump into mud puddles, visit the zoo or play with their friends. Through fun and sometimes nasty situations, Peppa and George discover the simple joys of life, learning to express their emotions and develop their vocabulary. The themes of friendship, family and learning are at the heart of each episode, offering young spectators valuable lessons while entertaining them. The series, which won a BAFTA Award in 2005 for its quality of animation, continues to captivate children from all over the world with its endearing characters and fantasy stories.
programme.desc-more: Peppa is a little slut full of life and energy, always ready to explore the world around her. programme.title: The future of the Great Barrier Reef
programme.desc: Under the surface of the Coral Sea, off the Australian Queensland, stands the world's largest coral reef, the Great Barrier. Every year, the arrival of spring in this underwater environment generates the magnificent and fragile reproduction of coral. More than 60,000 sea turtles are heading to Raine Island to make it the largest spawning site in the world. Processes as magical as they are threatened by global warming. This documentary offers us an immersive journey into the frenzy of the beginning of life, accompanied by enlightening explanations from local marine explorers and curators.

programme.title: Peppa Pig
programme.desc: Peppa is a small sow full of life and enthusiasm that makes the joy of its entourage. Every day is a new adventure for her and her little brother George, who accompanies her in her games and discoveries. Together, they explore their colorful world, meeting friends like Suzy Sheep and Danny Dog, while learning valuable lessons about friendship, family and creativity. Peppa loves to dress up and imagine fantastic stories, whether it's playing with the school mistress or turning into a superhero. Outdoor getaways, including the inevitable jumps into mud puddles, bring a touch of joy and laughter to their days. Accompanied by Mom Pig and Papa Pig, who support and encourage them, Peppa and George discover the simple pleasures of life while cultivating a spirit of adventure and camaraderie.
programme.desc-more: Peppa is a little slut full of life and energy, always ready to explore the world around her. programme.title: The fabulous history of birds, dinosaurs among us
programme.desc: Daniel Field, a specialist in paleo-ornithology at Cambridge University, is working on the reconstruction of the major stages of bird evolution, the last survivors of the disaster that led to the extinction of their cousins dinosaurs. In 2019, he found in a fossil the crane of the oldest modern bird ever discovered. Now, research focuses on the reasons for their survival for millions of years and on their colonization of our planet. However, many of the 11,000 species of birds that inhabit the Earth today are threatened with extinction.

Winning return for the kitchen of old
programme.desc: Once put in the old grimoires, the recipes of old make a frantic return today on social networks, in bookstores and in starred restaurants. programme.title: The Rookie: Los Angeles Cop
programme.desc: Discover the summary of the season 8 episodes of The Rookie: Los Angeles cop's series
programme.desc-more: Recently divorced and faced with a major turning point in his life, John Nolan (Nathan Fillion), a man aged 40 years, finds himself somewhat lost after his son left for university. On an ordinary day, he became a witness to a bank robbery where he barely escaped death. This traumatic event leads him to a profound introspection on his life choices and the path he wishes to take. Driven by a strong desire to change his life, John decided to leave his old life behind and settle in Los Angeles to fulfill his dream of becoming a policeman. As a new LAPD member, he must navigate in a complex environment where danger and stress are pervasive. At the earliest age of recruits, he found himself under the wing of Talia Bishop (Alyssa Diaz), his educational determination, who would have to help him overcome the specific challenges associated with his unique situation. Between training events, police intrigues and the need to prove its worth to younger colleagues, John Nolan will have to show courage and resilience while finding his place in a constantly changing world.

programme.title: The Rookie: Los Angeles Cop
programme.desc: Officer John Nolan (Nathan Fillion), now an instructor, is facing a troubling past when he again crosses the road of the formidable Rosalind Dyer serial killer. The latter, always wanting to make Nolan understand that their accounts are not settled, threatens to plunge him into a spiral of chaos. At the same time, his colleagues Timothy Bradford (Eric Winter) and Lucy Chen (Melissa O'Neil) are sent on a cover mission to Las Vegas, where they have to infiltrate a notorious criminal gang, putting their lives at risk. As this fifth season unfolds, tensions are rising and unexpected alliances are formed, notably through several crossovers with characters from the derived series, The Rookie: Feds. The stakes have never been so high for Nolan and his team, who must navigate between loyalty, danger and the shadows of their past.

programme.desc: Discover the summary of the season 8 episodes of The Rookie: Los Angeles cop's series
programme.desc-more: Recently divorced and faced with a major turning point in his life, John Nolan (Nathan Fillion), a man aged 40 years, finds himself somewhat lost after his son left for university. On an ordinary day, he became a witness to a bank robbery where he barely escaped death. This traumatic event leads him to a profound introspection on his life choices and the path he wishes to take. Driven by a strong desire to change his life, John decided to leave his old life behind and settle in Los Angeles to fulfill his dream of becoming a policeman. As a new LAPD member, he must navigate in a complex environment where danger and stress are pervasive. At the earliest age of recruits, he found himself under the wing of Talia Bishop (Alyssa Diaz), his educational determination, who would have to help him overcome the specific challenges associated with his unique situation. Between training events, police intrigues and the need to prove its worth to younger colleagues, John Nolan will have to show courage and resilience while finding his place in a constantly changing world.

programme.title: Cancer: Life ahead
programme.desc: The announcement of cancer is a life-changing event, but it does not stop it. The disease is no longer a condemnation: medicine is moving forward quickly, already healing 67% of patients, with the hope of reaching 80% by 2040, as announced by the Gustave Roussy Institute. In the face of this scientific revolution, our gaze on this evil must change. Celebrities - Florent Pagny, Carla Bruni, Jarry, Yaël Braun-Pivet, Alice Detollenaere and Camille Lacourt among others - and anonymouss - Adrien, surrounded by his family, Osvaldina, Etienne, Virginie and his two sisters - share their intimate fight with courage, without any taboo or false appearance.

programme.title: Miracle Operations: When Doctors Give Hope Back
programme.desc: Three French patients are being upset by their fate thanks to unprecedented medical achievements. Deborah, born without a uterus, receives the mother's birth and gives birth to her child. She became the first woman in France to give birth to a child after a uterus transplant. Priscilla, amputated with both hands and feet, after a medical error, has a transplant of both hands in the United States. Finally, Thibault, a tetraplegic after a fall, manages to move through an exoskeleton controlled by thought. 64 electrodes analyse his brain activity and transmit his motion intentions to a computer integrated into the exoskeleton. A global medical breakthrough that gives hope to millions of patients paralyzed around the world.

programme.title: Anonymous Brigade
programme.desc: After finding his daughter, Castaneda became a media figure. He received a visit from Mr. Balardi, who had been worried since his 15-year-old Stella, no longer gave a sign of life. Did she join her older sister, missing two years ago? Castaneda brings together members of his anonymous brigade and starts looking for him. Charlie quickly discovered that Stella posted charming photos on the internet and contacted the last man who posted a comment on one of her photographs. In parallel, the police are seeking information to bring down Castaneda.

programme.title: The Rookie: Los Angeles Cop
programme.desc: Discover the summary of the season 8 episodes of The Rookie: Los Angeles cop's series
programme.desc-more: Recently divorced and faced with a major turning point in his life, John Nolan (Nathan Fillion), a man aged 40 years, finds himself somewhat lost after his son left for university. On an ordinary day, he became a witness to a bank robbery where he barely escaped death. This traumatic event leads him to a profound introspection on his life choices and the path he wishes to take. Driven by a strong desire to change his life, John decided to leave his old life behind and settle in Los Angeles to fulfill his dream of becoming a policeman. As a new LAPD member, he must navigate in a complex environment where danger and stress are pervasive. At the earliest age of recruits, he found himself under the wing of Talia Bishop (Alyssa Diaz), his educational determination, who would have to help him overcome the specific challenges associated with his unique situation. Between training events, police intrigues and the need to prove its worth to younger colleagues, John Nolan will have to show courage and resilience while finding his place in a constantly changing world.

programme.title: The Rookie: Los Angeles Cop
programme.desc: Officer John Nolan (Nathan Fillion), now an instructor, is facing a troubling past when he again crosses the road of the formidable Rosalind Dyer serial killer. The latter, always wanting to make Nolan understand that their accounts are not settled, threatens to plunge him into a spiral of chaos. At the same time, his colleagues Timothy Bradford (Eric Winter) and Lucy Chen (Melissa O'Neil) are sent on a cover mission to Las Vegas, where they have to infiltrate a notorious criminal gang, putting their lives at risk. As this fifth season unfolds, tensions are rising and unexpected alliances are formed, notably through several crossovers with characters from the derived series, The Rookie: Feds. The stakes have never been so high for Nolan and his team, who must navigate between loyalty, danger and the shadows of their past.

programme.title: Helloween : Summer Breeze 2026
programme.desc: A major figure in power metal, the German band Helloween celebrates four decades of an exceptional career on stage.

programme.title: Metavers - virtual abuse, real dangers
programme.desc: Minecraft, Fortnite or Roblox: these online games total several hundred million monthly users. Considered by some users as an extension of themselves, these virtual universes are a real alternative to real life, in which one can build a new character and interact with others. But, popular with very young players, they are also the ideal ground for child criminality or neo-Nazi extremists. In the face of inaction by companies and public authorities, young militant users are themselves trying to regulate a world without faith or law.

programme.title: Catherine Deneuve, in her image
programme.desc: Trying to sflash off Bunuel's archetypal She has foiled her icon status by sometimes daring comedy, with Jean-Paul Rappeneau or François Ozon, or sailing in the cinema of Manoel de Oliveira and Raúl Ruiz, until Bernadette Chirac's most recent unexpected biopic. The directors who directed it - André Téchiné, Arnaud Desplechin, Benoît Jacquot, Nicole Garcia, Hirokazu Kore-eda... - mix with the actress's own voice to outline an out-of-standard course.

programme.title: Waterfalls: Power and Righing
programme.desc: From impressive Victoria Falls to the founding waterfall of the Eastern Mediterranean, waterfalls all over the world are fascinated by their beauty and power.

programme.title: Ecuador, at the top of biodiversity: From Amazonia to Andean volcanoes
programme.sub-title: From the Amazon to the Andean volcanoes
programme.desc: Ecuador is a country with an exceptional wildlife, both in the Galapagos and on the continent. In the Amazon forest, there are amazing species such as red ara, huppy hoazin and white-fronted capuchin. Going west, the landscape changes with the Andes Cordillera, where volcanoes, glaciers and valleys can be seen. Wildlife is also spectacular, with species such as nozzles, condors, puppy caracaras, collared bears, Andes deer and vicuñas. However, these biotopes are increasingly threatened by global warming.

programme.title: Ecuador, at the top of biodiversity: From the high Andes to the Galápagos Islands
programme.sub-title: From the high Andes to the Galápagos Islands
programme.desc: The Andes Cordillera in Ecuador is home to a rich fauna, with over 850 species of birds and species specific to the Galapagos Islands. The high-altitude forests of the Cordillera are the home of the masked trogon and the guacharo caves. The vast coastal plain is covered with humid forests where the mantle-screamer lives. The Galápagos Islands are a sanctuary for unique animals such as marine iguanas and giant Galapagos turtles.

programme.title: Louise Bourgeois, sculpture and anger
programme.desc: Through the words and voice of the French plastician and sculptor Louise Bourgeois (1911-2010), exploring her long career. It is a face-to-face with matter, a life of creation to exorcise the past, to tell each other. Portrait of an immense artist at work, whose life and work are confused.

programme.title: Universities around the world
programme.desc: Located in the heart of the Latin Quarter, the Sorbonne has seen Victor Hugo, Marie Curie, Jean-Paul Sartre or Simone de Beauvoir parade.

programme.title: Twist
programme.sub-title: 90s : A lifestyle that smells good nostalgia

programme.title: Viking myths
programme.desc: Myths are the foundation of our culture. It is all about love, war, betrayal, ambition, the struggle for freedom, sacrifice, happiness, transgression, the place of destiny... After Les Grands Myths, let's discover the mythology of the Far North, which has been a rich source of art history and pop culture.
programme.desc-more: The gods Thor, Odin and Loki, the giants, the elves and the dwarfs, the Ragnarök: François Busnel explores the myths and legends of the ancient Vikings.
programme.desc: The gods Thor, Odin and Loki, the giants, the elves and the dwarfs, the Ragnarök: François Busnel explores the myths and legends of the ancient Vikings.

programme.title: Cuisines of the terroir
programme.desc: In East Germany, not far from Dresden, Danilo Braun and his wife Katja run an oil mill. Just pressed, the flax oil has a taste of hazelnut and butter, perfect for accompanying a plate of potatoes and fresh cheese, typical dish of the region. Danilo also adds a fillet in its fruity smoothies or on a slice of toast. Like flax, hemp is rich in omega-3, fatty acid that the body cannot make. Katja uses this plant in all its forms: oil in ice cream that it decorates with roasted seeds. To enhance the product in its entirety, the Saxon couple reduces the meal, a solid residue of oil extraction, into flour. Katja then transforms it into homemade pasta, a base for a succulent vegetable salad.

programme.title: Ghana, coffins celebrate life
programme.desc: In Ghana, members of the Ga community, mainly present in Accra and its surroundings, are responsible for funeral practices now known throughout the world: the fancy coffins. Figurative volunteers, these unique pieces are there to represent a profession, memories, a symbol.

programme.title: The fabulous adventure of amphibians

programme.title: Interstellar
programme.desc: In the near future, the Earth is ravaged by environmental disasters, with persistent drought and devastating famine. Cooper (Matthew McConaughey), a former NASA pilot who became a farmer, struggles to raise his two children in this declining world. His life changes when he discovers mysterious coordinates in binary language, revealed after a sandstorm. Following these indications with his daughter Murph (Jessica Chastain), they find themselves in a NASA secret centre, led by Professor Brand (Michael Caine) and his daughter Amelia (Anne Hathaway). The latter reveals a bold project: sending a team into space in search of new living planets. While Cooper is selected for this perilous mission, he has to face up to heartbreaking choices, between his duty to humanity and his love for his children, while navigating through the mysteries of space and time.

programme.title: America: The New History of the First Men
programme.desc: From the Canadian North to the southern tip of Chile, through the southern United States, central Mexico and Brazilian Mato Grosso, new archaeological discoveries that are consistent, but still controversial, have brought to light a new paradigm in the archaeology of American prehistory: the appearance of the first humans on the continent could be nearly 30,000 years B.C.E., about 15,000 years earlier than the commonly accepted and taught thesis. If there were in the past some free-snipers to contest the scenario that the first ancestors of the Americans would have arrived on foot through Bering Strait 16,000 years ago, they were long kept out of the scientific community.

programme.title: Shutter Island
programme.desc: In 1954, two police officers investigated the mysterious disappearance of a woman who was detained in a psychiatric detention centre on Shutter Island.
programme.desc-more: In 1954, off the coast of Massachusetts, Shutter Island stood like a threatening shadow, beaten by winds and sprays. The island, which is home to a high-security psychiatric hospital, is the last refuge for the most dangerous criminals, those who society has preferred to forget. Between the thick walls of the establishment, where the screams of the patients mix with the sound of the waves, an atmosphere of mystery and paranoia reigns supreme. When Rachel Solando, a murderer interned for drowning her three children, disappeared without leaving any trace, the federal authorities sent two marshals to elucidate this troubling riddle: Teddy Daniels (Leonardo DiCaprio), a man haunted by his demons and a soldier's past marked by the horrors of the Second World War, and Chuck Aule (Mark Ruffalo), his new partner, as methodical as reserved. When they arrive on the island, Teddy and Chuck feel something is wrong. The staff, led by Dr. Cawley (Ben Kingsley), are too cooperative, too polite, as if he were hiding a much darker truth. Patients whisper incomprehensible warnings, doors lock for no reason, and the escaping eyes of the guards betray a silent conspiracy. The only clue in their possession? A mysterious piece of paper, slipped into Rachel's cell, where a series of numbers and letters seem to hide a coded message. For Teddy, this disappearance is not a simple escape, but the symptom of a much deeper malaise, perhaps linked to prohibited experiments conducted in the hospital basement.

programme.title: Gravitational waves: the signal of origins
programme.desc: A review of a major astrophysics phenomenon, predicted by relativity but measured for the first time in 2015, which could shed light on the origins of the cosmos.

To review this scientific event, the director met with researchers, including the LIGO, an American observation centre, where Rainer Weiss, Barry C. Barish and Kip Thorne, are working in 2017 to receive the Nobel Prize in Physics.

Today, the African-American community is mobilized as never before to thwart the electoral redistribution carried out by Republicans in advance of these elections. Tennessee is one of the seven states where Donald Trump's party has redesigned the electoral map in his favour. The Democrats have responded and done the same in California and Utah. But it was the Republicans - and by far - who won this war of redistribution. It should allow them to take up about ten seats in Congress. One in ten American voters changed their ridings during these reshuffles.

programme.title: Dracula: the true story
programme.desc: In the 15th century, Romanian prince Vlad Tepes terrified his enemies by his cruel empalations, inspiring much later the famous myth of Dracula.
programme.desc-more: Born under the pen of the Irish writer Bram Stoker, Dracula has haunted imaginations for more than a century. But behind the myth lies a Romanian prince who shook Europe in his time: Vlad III, prince of Valachie, also known in his time as Vlad Tepes. Thanks to the recent invention of the printing press, the more or less amplified narratives of its crimes spread to the west of the continent, where they serve as a support for a new imagination that will last for centuries. Together with researchers, this documentary, illustrated with red scenes made in rotoscopy, iconographic representations and animated maps, is part of the traces of the real Dracula.

The Galápagos Islands are a sanctuary for unique animals such as marine iguanas and giant Galapagos turtles.

programme.title: Interstellar
programme.desc: As the Earth is dying, explorers are leaving for a perilous space mission to find a refuge for humanity.
programme.desc-more: In the near future, the Earth is ravaged by environmental disasters, with persistent drought and devastating famine. Cooper (Matthew McConaughey), a former NASA pilot who became a farmer, struggles to raise his two children in this declining world. His life changes when he discovers mysterious coordinates in binary language, revealed after a sandstorm. Following these indications with his daughter Murph (Jessica Chastain), they find themselves in a NASA secret centre, led by Professor Brand (Michael Caine) and his daughter Amelia (Anne Hathaway). The latter reveals a bold project: sending a team into space in search of new living planets. While Cooper is selected for this perilous mission, he has to face up to heartbreaking choices, between his duty to humanity and his love for his children, while navigating through the mysteries of space and time.

programme.title: America: The New History of the First Men
programme.desc: New discoveries reveal the arrival of humans on the American continent nearly 30,000 years before our Common Era, questioning the record that had been accepted until then.
programme.desc-more: From the Canadian North to the southern tip of Chile, through the southern United States, central Mexico and Brazilian Mato Grosso, new archaeological discoveries that are consistent, but still controversial, have brought to light a new paradigm in the archaeology of American prehistory: the appearance of the first humans on the continent could be nearly 30,000 years B.C.E., about 15,000 years earlier than the commonly accepted and taught thesis. If there were in the past some free-snipers to contest the scenario that the first ancestors of the Americans would have arrived on foot through Bering Strait 16,000 years ago, they were long kept out of the scientific community.

programme.title: Dracula: the true story
programme.desc: Born under the pen of the Irish writer Bram Stoker, Dracula has haunted imaginations for more than a century. But behind the myth lies a Romanian prince who shook Europe in his time: Vlad III, prince of Valachie, also known in his time as Vlad Tepes. Thanks to the recent invention of the printing press, the more or less amplified narratives of its crimes spread to the west of the continent, where they serve as a support for a new imagination that will last for centuries. Together with researchers, this documentary, illustrated with red scenes made in rotoscopy, iconographic representations and animated maps, is part of the traces of the real Dracula.

programme.desc: Three years after the escalation of the Nagorny Karabakh conflict between Armenia and Azerbaijan, this documentary provides an overview of the situation and a breakdown of the challenges in this region of the South Caucasus.

programme.title: Poison
programme.desc: Ten years after their separation, a man and a woman find themselves at the grave of their young son. Adapted from a play, an intense marital drama in camera, with Tim Roth (Lucas) and Trine Dyrholm (Edith).

programme.title: Lindy hop: Log out and meet
Cells, in the heart of the living
programme.sub-title: At the source of vital energy
programme.desc: Why are we getting older? Can we slow down biological aging? Cell research is now exploring the mechanisms of division, energy production and aging. Some molecules could slow down cell degradation and prolong life. The story of Towana Looney, one of the first patients to receive a genetically modified pig kidney, illustrates the promise and risks of these new approaches. Researchers are also trying to save the white northern rhinoceros by creating germ cells from their skin. Progress that raises an essential question: how far can we get on the living?

programme.title: America owes her name: Amerigo Vespuccii
programme.desc: A figure of the era of great discoveries, Amerigo Vespucci was one of the most famous explorers of his time. Born of a family of Florentine notables who gave him a humanist education, he moved to Seville in 1490 and worked on two trips by Christopher Columbus, with whom he became friends. Fascinated by the discoveries of the 15-year-old navigator his elder, he decided to sail in his turn. As he goes along the coasts of Brazil, seeking a passage to the Indies, Amerigo Vespucci is won by a deep conviction, which will never leave him again: this is a new world. Combining historical interviews and reconstructions, this documentary portrait gives the story of an unknown character whose name is known to everyone.

programme.title: Newfoundland, stay or leave?
programme.desc: In Canada, residents of a fishing village on the Island of Newfoundland are invited to leave the site because of the cost of infrastructure.

programme.title: Travel to the kitchen
programme.desc: In Martinique, chef Guy Ferdinand prepares the famous culrané chicken. A geographer deciphers the origin of the term and the historical context of the island. Then, a visit to the Fort-de-France market allows you to discover local products such as dog sauce.

programme.title: Invitation to travel
programme.desc: Spain, words of women behind closed shutters - Scotland, witch revenge - Greece, raisin donuts - Poland, union of a woman and forest.

programme.title: Invitation to travel
programme.desc: Florence, Tchaikovsky white swan - In India, the absolute pacifism of the Jain - In Thailand, the Curry of Nu - In Belgium, a train and three heroes.

programme.title: America: The New History of the First Men
programme.desc: From the Canadian North to the southern tip of Chile, through the southern United States, central Mexico and Brazilian Mato Grosso, new archaeological discoveries that are consistent, but still controversial, have brought to light a new paradigm in the archaeology of American prehistory: the appearance of the first humans on the continent could be nearly 30,000 years B.C.E., about 15,000 years earlier than the commonly accepted and taught thesis. If there were in the past some free-snipers to contest the scenario that the first ancestors of the Americans would have arrived on foot through Bering Strait 16,000 years ago, they were long kept out of the scientific community.

programme.title: Poilão, the island sanctuary of Guinea-Bissau
programme.desc: The small island of Poilão, off the coast of Guinea-Bissau, has remained a sacred land for the inhabitants of the region for thousands of years. Bathed by the Atlantic, this preserved microcosm is home to an exceptional fauna: green turtles that have come to breed there, fiddle crabs, vultures, chameleons, varans and birds with flamboyant plumages.

programme.title: The Count of Monte Cristo: Treason
programme.desc: In 1815 Edmond Dantès (Jean Marais), a promising young sailor, took command of the ship Pharaoh after the death of his captain. While he stopped at the island of Elbe to deliver a message to Napoleon, his return to Marseilles was marked by intense joy, as he was about to marry his beloved, Mercedes (Lia Amanda). However, the jealousy of Fernand (Roger Pigaut), Mercedes' cousin, and the machinations of other conspirators, who see him as a threat to their ambitions, lead to his betrayal. Accused of Bonapartism, Dantès was imprisoned at the sinister castle of If, where he endured years of suffering. In this isolation, he discovered a plan of escape and met a former prisoner, Abbé Faria, who transmitted him with valuable knowledge. Once free, Dantès turned into a Count of Monte Cristo, determined to orchestrate a relentless revenge against those who destroyed his life.

programme.title: The Count of Monte Cristo: Revenge
programme.desc: Dantes, now known as Count de Monte-Cristo, returns to Paris with one goal in mind: revenge. He was supported by his faithful companion Jacopo, and immerse himself in the Parisian world where he discovered that his former rival, Fernand (Roger Pigaut), had become General Count of Morcerf and Mercedes's husband (Lia Amanda), his former love. By saving Fernand from a rixe, Dantès crossed the path of Albert (Jean Marais), the son of Mercedes, who did not doubt the true identity of his savior. Although Mercedes recognizes her former fiancé as Dantes, she is torn between her past and her present, refusing to flee with him. As Dantès weaves his web of revenge, he must navigate a world of betrayal, secrets and confrontations that will test his convictions and his desire for justice.

Its author, Shepard Fairey, street artist and a fervent opponent of President Trump, proposes a version of Lady Liberty as human as it is contemporary. Presented by Sonia Devillers, the magazine that analyzes images of our times.

There, John met a desperate painter, Michel, and a mysterious young woman, Nelly, under the cup of Zabel, a little malfrat who was to be honorable. Jean falls under Nelly's spell.

programme.title: Jean Gabin : War is not cinema
Cluedo
programme.desc: Six people are invited to dinner at the Manoir des Collines. They are greeted by Wadsworth, the hotel master, who calls them by a pseudonym. The evening is tense, because the guests don't know who brought them together. After the mysterious Mr. Moore arrived, Wadsworth revealed that all guests were victims of blackmail from Moore. The tone is rising. Moore then offered each guest a weapon and pushed them to kill Wadsworth, who locked them in the mansion. The lights then suddenly go out. When they turn on again, Moore died.

programme.title: The story of "Scenario"
programme.desc: During the summer of 2018, a few months after the presentation of his last film, Le livre d'image, at the Cannes Film Festival, Jean-Luc Godard submitted to Arte's production teams his new project entitled "Scenario". From there, the director of A blush, exchanges, for several months, with the channel, on what should become his next film. But it becomes clear to the filmmaker that this project will never be completed, and with the intervention of his close collaborators, Godard designs a final short film, whose design is filmed.

programme.title: Carole King and James Taylor : Live at The Troubadour
programme.desc: The moving reunions of two American music legends: in 2007, Carole King and James Taylor were again playing the scene of the Los Angeles Troubadour, where they gave their first concert together almost four decades earlier.

programme.title: Ecuador, at the top of biodiversity: From Amazonia to Andean volcanoes
programme.sub-title: From the Amazon to the Andean volcanoes
programme.desc: Ecuador is a country with an exceptional wildlife, both in the Galapagos and on the continent. In the Amazon forest, there are amazing species such as red ara, huppy hoazin and white-fronted capuchin. Going west, the landscape changes with the Andes Cordillera, where volcanoes, glaciers and valleys can be seen. Wildlife is also spectacular, with species such as nozzles, condors, puppy caracaras, collared bears, Andes deer and vicuñas. However, these biotopes are increasingly threatened by global warming.

programme.title: Ecuador, at the top of biodiversity: From the high Andes to the Galápagos Islands
programme.sub-title: From the high Andes to the Galápagos Islands
programme.desc: The Andes Cordillera in Ecuador is home to a rich fauna, with over 850 species of birds and species specific to the Galapagos Islands. The high-altitude forests of the Cordillera are the home of the masked trogon and the guacharo caves. The vast coastal plain is covered with humid forests where the mantle-screamer lives. The Galápagos Islands are a sanctuary for unique animals such as marine iguanas and giant Galapagos turtles.

programme.title: Cuba, the big return of boxers
programme.desc: At 47, former Namibian boxer Flores Rodriguez is too old to participate actively in international competitions. She now wants to create a boxing stable for women in Havana – a first in Cuba. The infrastructure is dilapidated, but it wants to do everything to prevent young athletes from failing because of unfavourable conditions: in Cuba, the simplest training opportunities and the right equipment are lacking.

programme.title: Chauvet Cave : In the footsteps of artists of Prehistory
programme.desc: Considered a masterpiece of Humanity, the Chauvet Cave is nicknamed the Sistine Chapel of Prehistory. Discovered 30 years ago, the hundreds of works that adorn its walls have changed our ideas about the evolution of art. One month a year, researchers have access to the ardéchis site to continue their investigations. Associated with recent technological advances - in particular photogrammetry, allowing the cave to be reconstructed in 3D -, the goldsmith work of archaeologists allows us to slip into the skin of our ancestors, to better decipher their ways of life and thought.

programme.title: Pauline Kergomard or the invention of kindergarten
programme.desc: By the end of the 19th century, new pedagogy changed the education of toddlers. From Friedrich Fröbel to Pauline Kergomard and Maria Montessori, the place of play, learning and autonomy of children is being rethought. Methods that continue to influence education today.

programme.title: School paths, paths of all dangers
programme.desc: In Kyrgyzstan, Sherali, 8, and Ali, 12, live with their grandparents in the Tian Shan mountain range, near the border with China. While in winter temperatures regularly reach 30 degrees, the two brothers face an hour and a half of donkey -back travel each morning to attend school. It's still dark when they get on their way.

programme.title: In Valencia, save photos of the flood
programme.desc: Hundreds of victims were killed by the centennial floods that devastated Valencia, Spain, in October 2024. And the mud flood also took away millions of photos, precious personal memories. Shortly after the disaster, a group of young people began to recover and restore these images that were believed to be lost. A million photos are still waiting to be saved.

programme.title: Hondo, the man of the desert
programme.desc: In a relentless sun, Hondo Lane (John Wayne), a lone adventurer and scout for the American army, arrives at a ranch isolated in Apache territory. This place is held by Angie Lowe (Geraldine Page), a courageous mother who alone raises her 10-year-old son, Johnny (Lee Aaker). As tension rises between the colonists and the Apaches, Hondo, aware of the dangers that threaten Angie and her child, decides to stay for a time to protect them. He tried to convince Angie to flee the area before it was too late, alerting the anger of the Apaches, who felt betrayed by the unfulfilled promises of the authorities. Angie, however, refuses to leave her land, determined to defend her home against external threats. Hondo then finds himself faced with a moral dilemma, drawn between his desire to help and respect for Angie's will, while the climate of tension grows around them.

programme.title: The fabulous adventure of amphibians
programme.desc: Amphibians have been deploying unsuspecting superpowers, changing lifestyles and appearances between land and water for 350 million years, as they are frogs, toads, axolotls or salamanders. In this episode, we discover that these vertebrates can push the boundaries between life and death.

programme.title: Below the images
programme.sub-title: Iran: Why Want the Head of Trump's Son?
programme.desc: On 11 November 2025, dozens of indigenous demonstrators attempted to access the COP30 website in Belém. The clashes with security officers have led to striking images that recall how climate change is particularly affecting indigenous minorities. Present on site, photojournalist Anderson Coelho, traces the confrontation he captured in images. Anthropologist Irene Bellier, an Aboriginal peoples specialist, reviewed the major moments of the climate conferences that served as the theatre for Aboriginal diplomacy.

programme.title: Faced with doubt
programme.desc: Nurse in a long-term care centre, Hana, 49, is a woman with a revealed and introverted temperament. Frustrated by her life, with financial difficulties and infernal cadence, Hana dreams of social success for her teenage daughter, whom she raises alone. The life of the quadrennial turns after the suspicious death of a patient in her service. Quickly accused of killing her, and then murdering other patients over the years, Hana finds herself caught in the middle of a media and judicial whirlwind. Inspired by real facts, this Czech miniseries dissects a media pack in a country where the rule of law is ceasing.
programme.desc-more: Nurse in a long-term care centre, Hana, 49, is a woman with a revealed and introverted temperament. programme.title: The Secret Life of British Gardens
programme.desc: It's the story of an idyllic English country garden located in the Lake District. Chris and Liz, the owners, love their outdoor space and do everything they can to promote wildlife. In spring, the garden is full of life: the orchard is in full bloom, the beds are full of bees and the pond is full of bridal parade tritons. Love is in the air! But the breeding season is short, and time is running out for the gardeners to find partners and start a family. At nightfall, a field mouse ventures right under the nose of the garden predators.

programme.title: Georgia: English, First Language
programme.desc: A very remote mountain region, Svanétie emptied of its inhabitants, went to look for a better life in the city. This exodus does not spare Kala, a village perched at 2,000 meters above sea level. A phenomenon that worries the school principal, attended by only 17 students. Here, because of the lack of teachers, certain subjects such as English might no longer be taught.

For him, as for the rest of society, Suzanne is just a potiche, an object of decoration without real utility. But fate, sometimes ironic, reserves surprises. programme.title: Shutter Island
programme.desc: In 1954, a woman in a psychiatric detention facility in Shutter Island disappeared. Her name is Rachel Solando and she's a very dangerous murderer. Two officers from the Federal Marshal Corps, Teddy Daniels and Chuck Aule, are coming to investigate the site. They discover the wet, hazy island off Boston where this very special prison hospital is located. Soon Teddy Daniels understands that the staff of the institution is hiding something. The only clue he has: a piece of paper on which is scratched a series of numbers interspersed with letters...
programme.desc-more: In 1954, off the coast of Massachusetts, Shutter Island stood like a threatening shadow, beaten by winds and sprays. The island, which is home to a high-security psychiatric hospital, is the last refuge for the most dangerous criminals, those who society has preferred to forget. Between the thick walls of the establishment, where the screams of the patients mix with the sound of the waves, an atmosphere of mystery and paranoia reigns supreme. When Rachel Solando, a murderer interned for drowning her three children, disappeared without leaving any trace, the federal authorities sent two marshals to elucidate this troubling riddle: Teddy Daniels (Leonardo DiCaprio), a man haunted by his demons and a soldier's past marked by the horrors of the Second World War, and Chuck Aule (Mark Ruffalo), his new partner, as methodical as reserved. When they arrive on the island, Teddy and Chuck feel something is wrong. The staff, led by Dr. Cawley (Ben Kingsley), are too cooperative, too polite, as if he were hiding a much darker truth. Patients whisper incomprehensible warnings, doors lock for no reason, and the escaping eyes of the guards betray a silent conspiracy. The only clue in their possession? A mysterious piece of paper, slipped into Rachel's cell, where a series of numbers and letters seem to hide a coded message. For Teddy, this disappearance is not a simple escape, but the symptom of a much deeper malaise, perhaps linked to prohibited experiments conducted in the hospital basement.

programme.desc: Born under the pen of the Irish writer Bram Stoker, Dracula has haunted imaginations for more than a century. But behind the myth lies a Romanian prince who shook Europe in his time: Vlad III, prince of Valachie, also known in his time as Vlad Tepes. Thanks to the recent invention of the printing press, the more or less amplified narratives of its crimes spread to the west of the continent, where they serve as a support for a new imagination that will last for centuries. Together with researchers, this documentary, illustrated with red scenes made in rotoscopy, iconographic representations and animated maps, is part of the traces of the real Dracula.

Through extracts of classics of cinema, behind-the-scenes film shoots and Hollywood testimonies, this film shows why zombies are always so timeless, and therefore as modern as ever: voracious, and contagious: it is the face of our revealed humanity.
